decision_rule.LOCK: v2.0 is locked on this arm's official numbers (whatever they are, provided the gating read is not HARMFUL) once cell PLANr reproduces them within the plan's own null; the lock record states the arm's SLU-F1 / intent, the per-scenario table, the frontier row and the module list (M1, M4b, M3, the RETIRED toolkit, E13, E22).

No row is ever filtered out of the scored manifest. Expected zero; the anchor side is provably zero (docs/receipts/slurp-finite-completion-exposure-v1.json).

planner_action_illegal. The flight's own count, the sample ids that carry it, and their action character counts and SHA-256 values (the form inherited from the B7a recovery note's section 8). This is the failure item E8c repaired; it is reported whether or not it is zero.

FIRST-REQUEST BYTE IDENTITY, stated honestly before contact. Under this arm the first request of a row (Perception) is NOT byte-identical to the base's: the slot-contract cards it carries are the v2 release's (M4b). What IS claimed and what the smoke proves: no request carries a tools array; the delivered answer of every row passed the normaliser node (one receipt per row); the Reviewer and Planner requests differ from the base's only through the upstream content.

NATIVE TASK-CONTRACT CALL COUNT against the anchor's realized 1,082, and the count of tool calls emitted by a role that holds no authority (expected zero; a non-zero count is not a failure of the flight -- the rail refuses the call and the episode continues -- but it is the single most interesting behavioural consequence of showing three more roles the tool definitions, and it is reported per role).

PER-SCENARIO intent and SLU tables over all 18 scenarios, in BOTH the natural-mixture and the equal-scenario weighting, plus net harmed rows per scenario with any scenario of five or more flagged (owner decision 17) -- a diagnostic the verdict must carry, not an additional gate.

resume_recovery_clause: owner decision 22 of 2026-09-18. If an attempt dies of an INFRASTRUCTURE failure with code and request bytes unchanged -- never a harness or config defect -- the one allowed recovery may be a RESUME-RECOVERY under item E10 instead of a re-fly: every complete row of the aborted attempt is kept without selection, every partial or unstarted row is flown under the same run id, and the merged manifest declares the predecessor attempt with its trace hash, kept-row list and that list's hash. It changes no question, roster, factor, comparator, decision rule or cap, and the run-cumulative budget must be re-checked because a resumed attempt and its predecessor share one run id. A resumed EFFICIENCY read must additionally state the split of its GPU hours and prefilled tokens across attempts, because a merged manifest's cost is the sum of two lease windows and a per-row rate computed over the merged manifest alone would be wrong.
